What we heard

The ask, and our answer

The Ask

Consolidate the product suite under one Northstar umbrella, before the Q4 launch.

Two core products today: Northstar, which generates the interface, and Atlas, the coding agent. Northstar Design and Northstar Loop form a cohesive branded house, and the system has to keep holding as the lifecycle fills in behind them.

  • A durable, long-term identity, not a launch skin
  • Unified visually unique and aggressively creative identity for the Northstar parent system
  • Distinct sub-brand systems for Design, Atlas, and Loop
  • An iconographic framework that expands
  • Voice, tone and messaging alongside the visual system
  • One design language and DNA across product UI and the marketing site
  • A handoff kit that your developer team can implement with full confidence
Our Answer

Strategic architecture first. Creative genius second.

We start with the IA and sub-brand logic: how Design and Loop sit under the parent, where Atlas lands, and what governs the stages that do not exist yet. The visual system and UX builds from that architecture, and deployment is kept clean and simple, governed by the research-based roadmap.

  • Branded-house pressure tested for all future states
  • A sub-brand relationship set rather than one-off identities
  • Full sub-brand system by Week 6, in time for the loud launch
  • Complete, documented, mastered system by Week 12
  • Handoff built for engineers: tokens, grids, spacing, semantics, etc.

AnswersR-03 · R-04 Order of operations

Three things we'd get right before anyone draws a mark

You told us previous agency relationships failed because they were transactional. In our experience that is usually a sequencing problem. Identity gets made before the architecture it has to serve is settled, so it breaks on the next product.

Sub-brand logic, pressure tested

A branded house is a decision, not a default. Do Northstar Design and Northstar Loop read as prefixed products, as descriptors, or as marks with their own equity? And where does Atlas land, arriving with recognition of its own? That decision governs every lockup and everything your team can add later without us.

A construction blueprint

With a roadmap that is explicitly open and forever evolving, we design the strategy for depth, color, logic, nomenclature, execution, flex, relationship, And/If/Or, and so on, so your team can continue to integrate and build from the same familial blueprint.

Anti slop

Your users are PMs, designers and engineers who are rightfully skeptical of generative sameness. The identity has to read as honed craft and content-restrained, to serve an audience that ships software for a living and can smell the difference.

AnswersR-01 What the system has to carry

One product, two categories, five phases

Northstar (Design) and Atlas (Loop) are the two overarching product functions today. The Product Factory is the vision to merge them into a self-contained product lifecycle. A new identity needs birthing to support this all in one closed loop system, spanning from Ideate to Loop.

Synthetic personas explore user problems and pre-game the market. The front door, reading social signal for enterprise-scale opportunities.

The collaborative canvas where AI and humans build high-fidelity UI together. Launched at I/O; exports to Figma and code.

Live today

Agents turn canvas mockups into verified, deployable components inside your existing repo. Atlas lives here, and this is where both categories meet.

Atlas ships today

The watchtower. Monitors live production for golden-path deviations and usage drift, which is what makes the loop self-improving.

AnswersR-01 · R-02 Phase 1 output

Three branded-house routes we'd put in front of you

Three architectures, each with a different center of gravity and a different answer to the same test: how each one absorbs Atlas. We would model all three against the real roadmap and recommend one by the first decision point.

Route A

Master brand

One dominant Northstar mark; sub-brands are typographic descriptors only. Maximum coherence, fastest to apply, cheapest to extend.

Trade-off: Design and Loop get little room to build their own equity with distinct user groups.
Our lean
Route B

System of marks

A parent mark plus a constructed sub-mark grammar: shared geometry, differentiated by a single controlled variable. Your team draws new stages from the rules.

Why we lean here: it's the only route where Ideate and Operate cost your team nothing to add.
Route C

Endorsed family

Northstar as endorser over more autonomous stage identities, each stage free to build its own equity with its own audience.

Trade-off: strongest for independent go-to-market, weakest at making the factory read as one loop.
How this closes

One route is selected at Week 3 and everything after is built from it. The routes are deliberately different systems rather than three finishes on one idea, so blending them is a new system rather than a revision. If the room wants elements of a route we did not select, we would rather hear it in Week 3 than in Week 6.

★ Visual gamification

Stars as a visible progress system, so a member can see exactly how close the next reward is. The progress bar and star set create positive reinforcement instead of an unexplained balance.

⚡ One-tap reorder

Still open

Eighteen asked and answered. Nine still live.

Your answers closed the architecture questions that mattered most: Northstar stands alone, the identity is bespoke, Atlas is in, and sign-off sits with one person. These are what is left, and each one still moves the work.

All9 Architecture3 Research2 Surfaces1 Governance3
ArchitectureDo you have a firm position on how Atlas lives within Northstar?

Atlas is in the family, which is settled. Whether it keeps its name, becomes a descriptor, or is absorbed outright is the largest decision left, and it governs every lockup we draw.

ArchitectureDo you envision the five phases being visually and operationally represented within the tool?

Ideate, Design, Build, Operate and Loop can be a story told about the platform, or a structure a user moves through. If they are surfaces, each needs a mark, a color position and a state, and the icon framework gets sized to match.

ArchitectureHow much room to grow should the system be sized for?

You defined success as room to grow. Three more pillars and eight are different systems. We would rather over-build the rules once than re-cut them in 2027.

ResearchHow far does the previous visual identity and user-base research feed our synthesis?

You said the prior identity will not be used. Seeing it, and the research behind it, still saves us a week of re-walking ground you have already covered. We would rather build on what you know than rediscover it.

ResearchWill we have access to key stakeholders for early interviews on aesthetic and taste goals?

You named a subjective element that is hard to write down, and the design lead's team built both products that are public today. Thirty minutes each with the people who hold that view beats a week of guessing at it.

SurfacesWhich marketing site is in question, or is it how Northstar is represented on the the client site site?

It changes what the Week 6 kit has to contain. A standalone site needs layout and component direction. A Northstar presence inside the client site needs a retrofit path that respects the the lab shell.

GovernanceBeyond the UX Design Lead, who else weighs in before a gate closes?

The brief names a single decision maker, which is the fastest structure we could ask for. If there are people behind that seat whose buy-in is needed, we would rather design the presentation for them from Week 1 than discover them at a gate.

GovernanceWhere are the hard the client brand constraints, and where is the latitude genuinely open?

the lab deliberately breaks standard the client branding, which is part of what makes this interesting. Knowing which rules are immovable and which are convention tells us how far the three routes can go before Week 3.

GovernanceIf Northstar graduates out of the lab, what survives: the name, the identity, or the architecture?

Most products that graduate end up in Cloud. We would rather design for that outcome now than have it decided for us later, because it changes how portable the system has to be.
